resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Pembine/Paust Tower record also describes a November 1933 International Stacey tower in Marinette County. Its original site (T37N, R20E, Sec. 36) differs from the survey description placing the Beaver tower in T31N, R19E, Sec. 10. The sources read do not link the two, so the story keeps them separate.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The build date (November 1933), design, and 2015 staffing end all come from NHLR alone. The 2015 date was not confirmed by a second source; WPR says the DNR will stop using all 72 towers but the copy read is undated, and a search snippet with a December 2015 date was not from a page read, so it is not used. Standing status rests on the firelookout.org directory, which gives no date. The survey station description (weebly copy) names the landowner; the name is deliberately omitted here and the quote uses only 'ON LAND OWNED'. The survey description is dated 1934 on the page read ('DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1934'); the story uses that date. Look-alike warning: the Pembine/Paust Tower (WHS HI234017) matches on month, year and architect (International Stacey Company). Its original site differs, but the record also says it was moved in 1991 to a current site whose location is not given on the page read; a duplicate check against the Beaver record may be worth doing. No access level is set: the We Wisconsin article's claim that only the Mountain tower is publicly climbable is not enough to say the Beaver tower is closed, and the survey description's gate and road directions were left out so as not to guide a visit. The brief omitted the 2015 staffing end; it is added here. Budget: 6 distinct pages read (one, WHS HI234017, is a different tower used for the look-alike note; the We Wisconsin and WPR pages are shared with the Bagley work) and 2 WebSearch.
